GhostwrAIter gets a new look and a new engine. This release redesigns all five screens, replaces the Gemini engine with Antigravity, and fixes defects that showed up in daily use without ever appearing in a report.

## Your posts are finally written for someone

Until now, the app sent **every** audience in your strategy to the model on each generation. On a strategy with four of them, that meant 2,355 characters of audience descriptions, several of which overlap and contradict each other. The result was an average of all your readers, which is to say written for nobody.

A **Target audience** field now sits next to the editorial pillar, on all three ways of creating an idea: manual entry, turning a news item into a post, and generating topics from your strategy. The model receives only the person you picked, with their vocabulary and their concerns.

The audience follows the post through its whole life: structure, hook, drafting, variants and the correction pass all aim at the same person. A corrected variant can no longer drift toward a different reader than the one the text was written for.

## A library that tells you what is left to do

The old list sorted your drafts by date. It never told you which one was closest to being published, and it never showed you a text.

The Library now reads as two panels: triage on the left, the **readable** post on the right, with LinkedIn's fold line drawn exactly where the platform will cut. You judge a draft by reading it, not by reading its metadata.

Three entries replace the chronological sort: **to review**, **ready**, **scheduled**. "Never reviewed" is stated plainly, because that is what blocks publication. Variants of the same topic are grouped instead of appearing as independent posts.

The metadata panel now shows version history, which had existed in the database since day one without appearing anywhere.

## New engine: Antigravity

Google replaced the Gemini command line with Antigravity. GhostwrAIter follows. If you had selected Gemini, your preference migrates automatically on first launch, with nothing to do.

All three engines remain available: Codex, Claude and Antigravity.

## Your text no longer runs under your machine's configuration

When you paste an article into "Turn a news item into a post", its content goes into the engine's prompt. Until now, that prompt ran with your local installation's settings, including any tools and connections you had authorized there for other purposes.

The app now pins its own policy on every call: read only, no external tools, machine configuration ignored, and an empty working directory. It asks for text, and the command line now says so explicitly.

## What no longer blocks

**The workshop no longer freezes.** When an engine failed, hit its quota or timed out, the screen stayed on the current step and the error message never arrived. Failures are now reported with their cause, and the timeout actually bounds execution.

**The bottom of screens is reachable.** Several pages did not scroll: their content extended past the window with no way to get to it.

**Keyboard focus is visible again.** The indicator that follows tabbing had become imperceptible in both themes.

**Search finds accented text.** A post containing "École" stayed invisible no matter how you typed it.

**The announced engine is the right one.** The app displayed "Codex" during generation even after another engine had been selected.

## Smaller fixes

- Premium correction now tells the truth: it no longer reports "corrected" on a text it did not improve.
- Copying a post reports failure instead of letting you paste something else.
- A created idea is no longer announced as a failure when only its refresh went wrong.
- Dialogs close with Escape and return focus to the button that opened them.
- The Cockpit counts today's publications in your local time zone, not in UTC.
- A setting that could not be saved no longer displays as active.
- Untitled ideas show their dated origin instead of an empty line.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. Your drafts, strategy and calendar are preserved. The database is upgraded on first launch.
